step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an employee expense management web application. Authentication flows through OpenID, ELB, ECS, and an auth Lambda. Users download a Single Page Application from ECS and interact with backend Lambdas for business logic, storing metadata in DynamoDB and file attachments in S3.

graph.name: GE Avio Expense Management Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless and containerized application for internal expense tracking.

nodes.name: Employee / User
nodes.notes: Internal company employees submitting expense tickets.

nodes.name: OpenID System
nodes.notes: Corporate identity provider for user authentication.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Load balancer handling incoming authentication traffic.

nodes.name: ECS Cluster
nodes.notes: Hosts single page application container and API gateway container.

nodes.name: Business Logic Lambdas
nodes.notes: 20+ Lambdas processing ticket actions and operations.

nodes.name: S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores financial document attachments encrypted with KMS.

edges.notes: User routes request through load balancer.
ELB forwards request to ECS container.
ECS invokes Lambda for authorization helper.
Auth Lambda verifies token against OpenID provider.
User downloads single page web app from ECS.
API gateway container routes requests to backend Lambdas.
Lambdas write ticket metadata to DynamoDB.
